panels.attribution_text: Rogowitz et al. Heart of lymphoma: primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma with endomyocardial involvement.. Case reports in oncological medicine 2013. doi:10.1155/2013/814291. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Cardiac MRI short axis T1 at the level of mitral valve reveals a large mediastinal mass infiltrating and obliterating the SVC causing SVC obstruction. The tumor extends into the right atrium (red arrow) and invades the tricuspid valve. Maximum diameter of the mediastinal mass measures 15 × 10 cm, and the mass in the right atrium measures 5.8 × 5.3 cm.

plate_findings.evidence: Primary mediastinal B cells (PMBC) associated with delicate interstitial fibrosis.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A shows a Hematoxylin and eosin stain of a mediastinal biopsy showing PMBC associated with delicate interstitial fibrosis, a classic pathological finding for Primary Mediastinal Large B-cell Lymphoma. B: Panel B shows immunohistochemical staining for CD20, demonstrating PMBC immunoreactivity, consistent with the diagnosis of PMLBCL as confirmed in the text. C: Panel C shows immunohistochemical staining for CD30, demonstrating PMBC immunoreactivity, consistent with the diagnosis of PMLBCL.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A is a CT scan of a 33-year-old female showing a large, lobulated soft tissue mass (92 x 50 x 64 mm) in the mediastinum, confirmed to be Primary Mediastinal Large B-cell Lymphoma based on the article title and caption, causing SVC obstruction. B: Panel B is a CT scan demonstrating the same mediastinal mass, which is consistent with the diagnosis of Primary Mediastinal Large B-cell Lymphoma.

panels.figure_caption: CT scan on presentation showing a mediastinal mass and concomitant obstruction of the SVC to 1 mm in diameter (green arrow).
in_text_mentions: A 33-year-old female, gravida 3 para 1 at 33 + 3-week gestation, presented with a five-day history of increasing bilateral upper limb swelling and orthopnoea. The pregnancy had been uncomplicated, and she had previously had one vaginal delivery at term. Chest computed tomography (CT) demonstrated a 92 × 50 × 64 mm soft tissue mediastinal mass obstructing the SVC to 1 mm diameter (Figure 1).

plate_findings.evidence: Diffuse neoplastic infiltration on a partially sclerotic background

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Pathological section showing diffuse infiltration of the mediastinal mass on a background suggestive of reactive fibrosis, consistent with Primary Mediastinal Large B-Cell Lymphoma. B: Histological observation of clear-cell morphology of the neoplastic B cells, a characteristic of this lymphoma. C: High-power view of tumor cell morphology, showing round nuclei and clear cytoplasm, consistent with PMBCL. This mass is described in the caption and article title as a large mediastinal mass characteristic of primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma, involving the left mainstem bronchus, pericardium, and left ventricle.

in_text_mentions: Upon initial evaluation, the patients' vitals were significant for tachycardia (110 bpm) and a chest CT was obtained demonstrating a large mediastinal mass (16 cm) narrowing the left mainstem bronchus and distal airway that involved the pericardium and myocardium of the left ventricle (Figure 2). At the time, there were no discernible physical signs indicative of cardiac tamponade, and the rest of the physical examination was normal. Preliminary lab work was significant for mild anemia (Hgb 11.0 g/dL) and thrombocytosis (Plt 488 103/μL).

in_text_mentions: A 26-year-old African American female patient with a history of asthma presented to the Emergency Department (ED) at a large tertiary care hospital with a productive cough featuring blood-tinged sputum, shortness of breath, and new-onset facial swelling. Initial evaluation included a neck CT, which revealed findings concerning for cellulitis and prevertebral soft tissue swelling. She was diagnosed with right upper lobe pneumonia and discharged with Augmentin and azithromycin. Figure 1 depicts the initial chest X-ray obtained on admission.

panels.rationale: HRCT demonstrates a large mass (PMLBCL) in the anterior mediastinum that is compressing and encasing the superior vena cava, leading to clinical symptoms consistent with SVC syndrome.

Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.93881. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: HRCT represents a large soft tissue mass in the anterior mediastinum, as pointed by the arrow. The mass appears to compress the superior vena cava. HRCT: high-resolution computed tomography
in_text_mentions: High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of the chest, as given in Figure 1, demonstrated a large anterior mediastinal mass compressing and partially encasing the SVC, correlating with the patient’s facial swelling and orthopnea. The mass displaced the heart and was associated with mild right pleural effusion, mediastinal lymphadenopathy, and patchy adjacent atelectasis, but no large recurrent pericardial effusion. A right-sided chest tube was placed for drainage of the pleural effusion, which yielded 1,000 mL of milky fluid within 12 hours.
